# rachel

39. BMI 45 at baseline. Knee osteoarthritis, both knees, the right one worse.
Five months into a GLP-1 prescription her GP started in February 2030. Two
kids, school-run life, a desk job she drives to. Synthetic; any resemblance to
a real person is accidental and unintended.

## In her own words

"I did not start the injections to get a personal best. I started because my
knees were making the decisions. The appetite thing is strange: I am not
being good, the food just stopped shouting. I want that written down
somewhere, because everyone assumes I am white-knuckling it and I am not.

The scale is fine, the scale goes down, whatever. The thing I actually check
is the stairs. Fourteen stairs at home. I was stopping at eight. Now it is
twelve of fourteen most days. When it is fourteen of fourteen with the
washing basket, that is my finish line, not a number.

I used to log food on the good days only. I know that. A 1400 day got
logged, a 2600 day did not. There is no point pretending the old diary means
anything."

## The record her life produces

- Fourteen months: nine months pre-medication baseline (2029-05-01 to
  2030-02-02), five months on medication (2030-02-03 to 2030-06-30).
- Weight twice a week from a connected smart scale (capture: connector).
- Intake from an app: 22 scattered days across the whole pre-medication
  period, all flattering; daily and involuntarily low (about 1100 kcal) once
  the medication starts.
- Sessions: short walks tracked by a phone app (vendor), aqua fitness typed
  in by hand, and a handful of walks she logs manually with round, generous
  durations.
- Medical: the knee episode with an athlete-stated restriction (no
  high-impact, stairs limited), and the medication row with athlete-stated
  expectations (appetite markedly reduced).
- Checks: the stairs test she chose herself, recorded as pass/fail with the
  fraction in the note because the schema cannot hold "12 of 14" as a value.

## The axis she stresses

Medication that changes the numbers involuntarily; capacity limits and
capacity goals; a body anchor that is not weight; coverage so one-sided that
before/after comparisons are unsafe; and the cleanest resolution-ladder test
in the corpus: the same walk described twice, once by her and once by her
phone, disagreeing by a factor of two.
